newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end higher.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end higher.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended higher on Tuesday in all months, due to technical buying from individual investors, local traders said.
Prices ranged from 60 to 180 yen higher, with the benchmark May 1998 contract closing 180 yen up at 14,380 yen per tonne.
The day's estimated trading volume was 29,867 lots.
All contracts rose from the opening, despite price falls in the Chicago corn market and the stronger yen. Traders said technical buying from local investors supported the market throughout the day.
The spot July contract expires on June 13. Position adjustment at the spot month will be a wild card until the end of this week, they said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.73-1/2 per bushel at 0745 GMT, down from $2.74 at Monday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.12-1/2 a bushel at 0745 GMT, up from $8.11 at Monday's close.
